text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT

- Governor of Finland's central bank, Sirkka Hamalainen, said bank will not need to intervene in interest rates if the government and interest groups give support to new system of fixed exchange rates.
- Defence ministry has urged military to create oportunities for women to become air force pilots.
- Nearly half all Finns, including opposition supporters, say the Lipponen government has done a good job, poll shows. @
- President Martti Ahtisaari praises the government's performance in linking the markka to the ERM, says it will not dramatically affect the Finnish economy.
- Old mill town Verla a candidate for UNESCO's world heritage list.
KAUPPALEHTI
- A big Nordic bank merger is still a possibility, says S-E Banken's Jacob Wallenberg. But no consolidation projects are under way, he says. @
- Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto says balanced state finances would be the best buffer against cyclical downswings.
- Asko looking to sell its Karhu ski manufacturing operations by year-end.
- Rettig has sold its eight percent stake in Finnlines for over 150 million markka.
- Estonian Kaubamaja department store plans to open shop in downtown Helsinki. Local merchants say they are not worried. @
AAMULEHTI
- Two big retailers, Stockmann and Anttila, are engaged in a virtual trade war, giving big price cuts to entice customers.
- Industrialists consider nuclear energy the only way to boost the country's power supply.
DEMARI

- Labour Minister Liisa Jaakonsaari says Finland should create a "job recycling" scheme like that of Denmark. Plan would coordinate various job training, job sharing and unemployment support programmes. @
- President Ahtisaari says United States' continued presence in Europe is important for European security.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Turku region's European Parliament candidates say they would be ready to pare down Euro-MPs' expense allowances.
- Green party says Finland's membership of European Economic and Monetary Union should be decided by a qualified majority in parliament, and not by a simple majority.
- Former adjutant of former president Mauno Koivisto says in memoirs that Koivisto has no skeletons in his closet.
